# `numbering.renumber`

<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask docs-gen` from crates/ew-commands/schemas/numbering.renumber.schema.json. Do not edit: change the source and regenerate. -->

`numbering.renumber` (`RenumberDevices`): renumbers device counters under the page-based scheme.

The devices in scope that take part in numbering (`numbering::numbered`: no terminal aspect, no frozen
tag, default scheme; with `include_frozen` also the frozen ones) and are placed are grouped by (page of
the main representation, letter). In each group the devices are ordered by their main representation's
position, column first (x, then y), then by ID. Counters held by devices of the group outside the scope
are reserved. Then, in order:

- `only_nonconforming`: a device keeps its counter unless it has none or shares it with an earlier
  device of the group (or a reserved one); those get the lowest free counter, one that no device of
  the group keeps and no earlier device was given;
- else with `close_gaps` (the default): each device gets the lowest counter that is neither reserved
  nor given to an earlier device, so the group reads 1, 2, 3 … in position order;
- else: as `only_nonconforming` (a device keeps a counter that is not reserved and not taken by an
  earlier device; the others get the lowest free one).

**Frozen tags.** Without `include_frozen` (the default) a device with a frozen tag is left alone. With
`include_frozen: true`, each frozen device in scope that the scheme numbers (placed, no terminal aspect,
default scheme) takes part like the others and is unfrozen: `TagSpec.frozen` is cleared, keeping no
literal, so its tag follows the numbering rule from then on; this explicit renumber, previewed and
undoable like every command, is the one user action that changes a frozen tag (doc 03 §8.6). A frozen
device in scope that the scheme cannot number (unplaced, a terminal, a `Child` or named scheme) keeps its
frozen tag, because without it the tag would print "?".

Only counters (and, with `include_frozen`, frozen tags) change: identities and every reference by ID
stay, so the topology is identical and no reference is orphaned (Golden B, FR-NUM-008). Running it
twice changes nothing the second time. Bulk. Outcome: none.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `include_frozen` | boolean | no | `false` | Renumber and unfreeze the frozen devices in scope that the scheme numbers (default false). |
| `options` | [`RenumberOptions`](#renumberoptions) | no | `{"close_gaps":true,"only_nonconforming":false}` | The options. |
| `scheme` | [`NumberingScheme`](#numberingscheme) | no | `"page_based"` | The scheme. |
| `scope` | [`DeviceScope`](#devicescope) | yes |  | The devices to renumber. |

## Types

### DeviceScope

Which devices `numbering.renumber` renumbers.

One of the following forms:

1. **Form 1**: The listed devices.

   Shape: object { `selection`: array of [`CmdUuid`](#cmduuid) }

   | Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | `selection` | array of [`CmdUuid`](#cmduuid) | yes |  |  |

2. **Form 2**: The devices whose main representation is on one of the pages.

   Shape: object { `pages`: array of [`CmdUuid`](#cmduuid) }

   | Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | `pages` | array of [`CmdUuid`](#cmduuid) | yes |  |  |

3. **Form 3**: Every device.

   Shape: `"project"`

### CmdUuid

A lower-case hyphenated UUID naming a record (doc 05 §3.2).

Type: string (at least 36 character(s), at most 36 character(s))

Pattern: `^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$`

### NumberingScheme

The numbering scheme.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `"page_based"` | `{page}{letter}{counter}`, counters unique per page of the main representation and letter. |

### RenumberOptions

Options of `numbering.renumber` (FR-NUM-009).

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `close_gaps` | boolean | no | `true` | Close counter gaps: counters become 1, 2, 3 … in order; otherwise a conforming counter is kept. |
| `only_nonconforming` | boolean | no | `false` | Renumber only devices without a counter or whose counter collides in their scope. |

## Exit codes

A command runs as one line of a command log replayed by `ew apply` ([doc 17 §3.5](https://github.com/Ironkode787/ElektraWatt/blob/main/docs/design/17-extensibility.md#35-command-logs-ewcmd)). The exit code of `ew apply` is:

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | The line committed as one transaction. |
| 1 | A prevent rule or the command's own domain rule refused the line (`Prevented`, `Rejected`); the lines before it stay committed. |
| 2 | Anything else stops the replay: invalid parameters, a missing record, an unresolvable reference, an open, lock or save error. |

The codes of every subcommand are in [doc 17 §3.2](https://github.com/Ironkode787/ElektraWatt/blob/main/docs/design/17-extensibility.md#32-exit-codes).

This is a bulk command: a log line runs it as a preview first and commits the previewed result ([doc 17 §3.5](https://github.com/Ironkode787/ElektraWatt/blob/main/docs/design/17-extensibility.md#35-command-logs-ewcmd)).
